name: Tekelyu Waterfall
full: Tekelyu Waterfall (Tekelyu), ~60 m high, on the Tekelyu River — a right tributary of the Akkem, ~8 km below Lake Akkem, in the Belukha area (Katun Range). NOTE: this is Ust-Koksa District, not Chemal District — no waterfall of this name near Chemal was found in the sources. It is visible from the Akkem trail (Tyungur — Lake Akkem) from the left bank of the Akkem; the approach to its foot is from the right bank (forded in autumn) or via the Oroktoy trail.
near: The village of Tyungur (the start of the Akkem trail; ~30–34 km along the trail — a calculation: the lake is 37.5–42 km from Tyungur, the waterfall ~8 km below the lake); the village of Kucherla (the start of the Oroktoy trail).
elev: Drop height ~60 m (all sources); elevation above sea level — not found (camps on the Oroktoy route ~2150 m, Tyungur ~850 m — mountainstories).
short: The second-highest waterfall in the Altai Republic (~60 m, after Rassypnoy): the Tekelyu River (“of the goats”) plunges almost vertically, without cascades, into the Akkem valley on the way to Belukha. A natural monument since 1996; reachable only on foot or on horseback, 2+ days.
desc: Tekelyu is a waterfall on the river of the same name, ~13 km long, a right tributary of the Akkem, about 8 km below Lake Akkem under Belukha (Katun Range, Ust-Koksa District). It is ~60 m high; unlike many Altai waterfalls, the water falls in almost a single vertical stream, which gives a sense of power. The name comes from the Altai “teke” (mountain goat), of which there are many here. It is a natural monument of republican significance (since 1996 — turistka, altai-poxod; sibalt gives 1980), within the territory of the Belukha nature park; species from the Altai Republic Red Data Book live here — the saker falcon, Altai snowcock, great rosefinch and great snipe. The waterfall is clearly visible from the Akkem trail from the left bank of the Akkem; opposite is a popular camp spot with flat places for tents and water. You can reach the foot by crossing the Akkem's channels (realistic in autumn at low water), then 30–40 min to the upper cascade; in summer the approach is possible via the Oroktoy trail from Kucherla through the headwaters of the Tukhman (a radial hike to the waterfall ~4 km, +130 m — mountainstories). Many tourists confuse it with sights near Chemal — there is no Tekelyu waterfall in Chemal District (there you have Che-Chkysh, Belter-Tuyuk and Kamyshlinsky).
guide: Tekelyu is visible right from the Akkem trail — look at the right bank of the Akkem about half a day before Lake Akkem: a white 60-metre string against dark rock. Stop at the camp opposite — it's one of the best overnight spots on the way to Belukha. If you go in September, you can wade across the Akkem's channels and climb to the upper cascade in 30–40 minutes; in July the water is high — don't take risks. Watch for mountain goats — “teke”, from which the waterfall got its name. Combine it with Lake Akkem, the Seven Lakes Valley and the view of Belukha.
see: The waterfall itself (from the left bank of the Akkem and at its foot); the upper cascade (30–40 min from the ford); the Akkem valley; further — Lake Akkem and the view of Belukha, the Akkem weather station, the Seven Lakes Valley (a radial hike of 12 km, +600 m — mountainstories); on the Oroktoy variant — Lake Kyuldyuayry, the Kuzuyak pass.
skip: You're looking for a waterfall near Chemal for a couple of hours — Tekelyu is in a completely different district, part of a multi-day hike to Belukha (2–3 days one way). You aren't ready for a ford and tents — look from the trail.
diff: Moderate: the Akkem trail is 37.5–42 km to the lake with a gain of ~1000–1977 m (activelife / sport-marafon — the sources differ), 2–3 days; fords. The Oroktoy trail is higher and harder (a day with +1050 m).
when: July — September; to the foot — in autumn (low water, the Akkem can be crossed — turistka, sibalt). The trekking season to Belukha runs from mid-June to September.
hours: Round the clock (a natural feature on the trail).
daytime: Morning — the slope is lit and there are fewer clouds; in the evening from the camp opposite — a silhouette at sunset (not confirmed).
how: To Tyungur: a bus Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur 10:00 → 17:50, Tue–Sun, from 3677 ₽, sole proprietor Maimanov I.Ya. (unitiki 2026); or to Ust-Koksa + a taxi of 50–60 min (belukha.ru); a group transfer from the airport 6000 ₽/person (June–August 2025, belukha.ru). Tyungur is 60 km from Ust-Koksa and 894 km from Novosibirsk (turistka). Then on foot along the Akkem trail: over the Kuzuyak pass to “Three Birches” (~17 km, can be done with a GAZ-66 transfer) and up the Akkem ~13–17 km to the camp opposite Tekelyu (calculation), and to the lake another ~8 km.
needcar: To Tyungur — yes; beyond that on foot/horseback; a GAZ-66 transfer to “Three Birches” shortens the route (turistka, sport-marafon).
self: Yes — the trail is popular and well worn (trekkingmania); Russian citizens need a passport (Ust-Koksa District is a border zone; an FSB permit is needed only in the 5-km strip, e.g. the Tomsk camps); foreigners need an FSB permit, processing 60+ days (sport-marafon). Register your group with the Ministry of Emergency Situations.
roadtype: To Tyungur — paved/dirt; Tyungur — “Three Birches” — a battered dirt road over the Kuzuyak pass (GAZ-66); then a footpath along the Akkem (forest, rocks, streams).
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk — Tyungur ~8 h; Tyungur — the camp opposite Tekelyu 1.5–2 days on foot (estimate; to the lake 2–3 days, sport-marafon); with a transfer to “Three Birches” — 1 day.
stay: A tent camp opposite the waterfall (flat places, water — altai-poxod); at Lake Akkem — the “Ak-Kem” weather station (since 1932, they bake flatbread for tourists; at the “Akkem” tourist base a banya costs 4000 ₽ for 3 h, no shower — varandej 2017), the “Akkem” mountain hut, the Active Life campsite (activelife.bz); in Tyungur — the “Vysotnik” tourist base (7 Zarechnaya St., +7 913 698-19-06, belukha.ru, 2GIS 4.6/70), the “Tyungur” base (turbazy.ru) — prices not found.
net: There is no signal on the trail or at the lake; the nearest is Tyungur/Kucherla (activelife, trekkingmania). You need a radio/satellite phone.
entry: The Belukha nature park is a regional protected area: since 01.07.2026 the fee is 300 ₽ (it was 100), unchanged for residents of the Altai Republic (Tolk 30.06.2026); how to pay — not found (possibly via the “Green Button”/checkpoints).
transfer: A bus to Tyungur from 3677 ₽ (2026); a group transfer 6000 ₽ (2025); a transfer to “Three Birches” — not found.
bring: Your passport, a tent and sleeping bag (frosts at night by the Akkem), trekking boots and sandals for fords, a rain jacket, gas (campfires are restricted), a first-aid kit, a filter, repellent, tick insurance, a radio/satellite communication.
warn: The Akkem fords are dangerous in July at high water; to the foot — only at low water. The border zone of Ust-Koksa District (passport; a permit for foreigners). In summer a border post at Lake Akkem checks documents and logs everyone; Russian citizens can go freely up to the glacier, beyond that is a strict border zone with a permit (guide-altai; varandej 2017). Ticks (in the Altai Republic by 25.08.2026 — 3600 bite reports, 22 cases of encephalitis). No signal. Bears in the Belukha area — store your food properly. Don't confuse it with Chemal District!
food: In Tyungur — local mountain honey and dairy from residents (turistka); at Lake Akkem — meals at the weather station/at the Active Life campsite (by order). No cafes with ratings were found.
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.7/5 (3 reviews), no. 2 in Ust-Koksa — “a real gift on the route”, a rainbow on a sunny day; no 2GIS/Yandex entries for the waterfall were found. The “Vysotnik” tourist base — 2GIS 4.6/70. Pros: a powerful vertical stream, the view from the trail, the camp opposite; cons: hard to reach the foot in summer.

p.sum: Tekelyu is a 60 m waterfall in the Akkem valley under Belukha (Ust-Koksa District, not Chemal). It is visible from the Akkem trail on the 2nd day of the trek from Tyungur; to the foot — fording in autumn or via the Oroktoy trail. A bus to Tyungur from 3677 ₽, then 1.5–2 days on foot.
